nodes.title: READ ME FIRST - How to use this workflow
widgets_values:
# MiniMax H3 - 2 Pass Music Video Workflow (VRGDG settings)

These are the **exact render settings used for the VRGDG Video Builder music videos** (2 Pass, 2K).

## Quick start
1. **Download the models** in the note to the right and restart ComfyUI.
2. In **3 - YOUR INPUTS**: load **Reference Image 1** (your character sheet) and **Reference Image 2** (your location).
3. Write your prompt in the **PROMPT** box. Image 1 is `<Subject 1>`, Image 2 is `<Subject 2>`, the song is `<Audio 1>`.
4. Set **Duration (seconds)**. H3 likes **5-12 s**. Above ~12 s most cards run out of memory.
5. Pick your audio with the **USE CUSTOM AUDIO** switch:
   - **ON (true)** = your own song/voice from the **Load Audio** box drives the video. Mouths lip-sync to it and it is the final audio.
   - **OFF (false)** = H3 makes its own sound (built-in audio). Describe the sound, dialogue or music in the prompt instead.
6. Press **Queue**. The video is saved to `ComfyUI/output/VRGDG_H3_2Pass/`.

## Good to know
- **Keep any audio file selected in Load Audio, even with the switch OFF.** ComfyUI checks that box before every run; it is simply not used when the switch is OFF.
- **Custom audio starts at 0:00.** Trim your song to the exact section you want first, the same length as Duration.
- **Seeds** are random every run (both passes). Set them to *fixed* to repeat a take.
- **Feedforward chunking** (purple nodes in 2 - MODELS) lowers VRAM. The Builder turns it on for clips **over 8 s**. For short clips you can bypass both (select, Ctrl+B) to render a bit faster.
- **No RTX card?** In 8 - OUTPUT change the resize method from `nvidia_rtx_vsr` to `lanczos`.

nodes.title: Model routing
widgets_values:
**Pass 1** = Singularity -> feedforward. No LoRA.

**Pass 2** = Singularity -> 8-step 768p Turbo LoRA (1.0) -> feedforward.

The purple feedforward nodes only lower VRAM. Bypass both (Ctrl+B) for short clips if you have VRAM to spare.

nodes.title: PROMPT (MiniMax H3 format)
widgets_values: subject_definitions: is the band's lead singer from the first character reference, a woman with a glossy cherry-red blunt bob with blunt bangs, winged eyeliner and deep red lipstick, silver spike earrings, wearing a sleeveless ivory high-neck top with sculptural folded-paper origami ruffles, a black corset belt, a pleated ivory and black skirt, a red cuff bracelet on one wrist, red tights, and black patent knee-high platform boots, gripping a sleek silver handheld microphone in one hand. is the grand civic theatre banquet hall from the second reference image, featuring a long banquet table with a cream tablecloth, folded napkins and tall silver candelabras, red velvet dining chairs, a crystal chandelier, tall windows with cream curtains, red damask walls, and a polished parquet floor. This reference defines the environment, lighting, and atmosphere, while the camera uses its own area of the space and places the characters in new positions within it.

nodes.title: Load Audio (your song - keep a file selected)
Inputs help
widgets_values:
**Duration**: seconds of video. The frame count is snapped to what H3 accepts automatically.

**Resolution**: 1920x1088 is what the Builder renders at 2K. Pass 1 runs at half size (960x544), the learned upscaler doubles it.

**Audio switch**: ON = Load Audio drives the video. OFF = H3 makes the sound.

nodes.title: AUTO - Duration to valid H3 frame count
AUDIO SWITCH - reference audio for H3
CUSTOM AUDIO - lock your audio into the latent
How the audio switch works
widgets_values:
**ON** - your audio is a reference for H3 *and* is locked into the starting latent, so the picture is generated to match it (lip-sync) and your audio is the final soundtrack.

**OFF** - no reference audio; H3 generates video **and** sound together, and the generated sound is decoded and saved with the video.
